unit: B1 first-process compilation time / TypeScript time
aggregation: Equal-source geometric mean of Evening and lexer B1/TypeScript ratios. Each ratio divides three-sample medians of import + API load + first checked direct-library request. Historical observations declare their own cohort and timing boundary.
formula: exp(mean(log(median(B1 import + API load + first request ms) / median(same-campaign TypeScript import + API load + first request ms))))
measurement_boundary: First ordinary checked direct-library request in a fresh worker, including host import and actual compiler API loading plus source loading, checking and emission. Private API-specific Base disk caches are primed before measurement. Excludes process startup, preparation, provenance checks, output validation and output saving. This is first-request latency, not a pristine cold CLI invocation or warmed steady-state throughput.

protocol: Pinned Node 24.18.0 on CPU3, three rotated fresh-process rounds per role/input. Private API-specific Base caches primed outside measurement. One first and three later checked-library requests per process in P57/P58; P56 records one first request. Each request uses fresh source syntax and must match its role's prepared module bytes. B1 and B2 are separate campaigns with separate TypeScript samples; 1GiB Node heap, 2GiB process-tree RSS ceiling, 4GiB available-memory floor.
limitations: Current headline measures installed B1. The larger Phase58 B2 gains belong to a different, self-emitted compiler image that is not installed.

Current first-process timing includes host import and API load. Historical P42–48 legacy request timing excluded host import and used a different output backend; the history is disconnected at that boundary.
P42–45, P47 and P48 also used different program cohorts. Do not interpret differences between disconnected averages as measured compiler improvements or regressions.
P57 and the P58 fresh baseline remeasure the exact Phase56 string01 B1 compiler. They are measurement observations, not new compiler releases.
Each B1 comparison uses its own campaign's TypeScript samples. B2's TypeScript samples must not be pooled into the B1 denominator.
Selected last01 B1 changes first-process time by -0.76% for Evening and +1.59% for lexer; the geometric aggregate is +0.40%. Three samples per cell do not establish significance.
Later-request sequences still warm up. Their aggregate (+0.50% time) is not a steady-state throughput estimate and is separate from the first-process headline.
API-specific Base disk caches are primed before measured workers. Preparation, provenance checks and inter-request output saving are outside the clocks but can affect process state.
Earlier Phase58 shared01 compiler measurements are not selected last01 results. B1 allocation was not remeasured for the final compiler.
Two selected sources do not estimate typical arbitrary-application compiler throughput. Earlier P8–24 check-only compiler-source observations remain a separate history.
